title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says Congress should not offer extra money or special regulatory aid to firms or financial institutions that are at risk of collapse because of AI market stresses. Instead, Congress should focus on helping all Americans who have been harmed by these risks.

title: To require an assessment with respect to the technical capacity of the Department of State to address the use of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to facilitate trafficking in persons.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
summary: This policy requires the Department of State to assess its technical capacity to address how artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies are being used to facilitate human trafficking. The goal is to strengthen the department’s ability to prevent, detect, and respond to tech‑enabled trafficking efforts.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 sets forth requirements to make AI systems safe, transparent, and trustworthy. It mandates that developers conduct rigorous testing, disclose risks, and follow oversight protocols to protect the public while fostering reliable AI research.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how it uses AI systems and to provide clear documentation on their design and operation. The law mandates reporting, oversight, and privacy protections to ensure veterans and the public can understand and trust the AI tools employed in VA services.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act seeks to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans' claims. It establishes requirements for transparency, oversight, and protection of veterans' rights to ensure fair and responsible AI decision‑making.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act aims to protect the integrity of elections by addressing potential threats from AI-generated deceptive content. It proposes regulatory measures to prevent AI-driven misinformation from influencing voter behavior and ensuring fair democratic processes.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to shield people from misleading or false claims made by AI systems. It sets clear rules and enforcement measures so that AI technology is transparent and accountable to consumers.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act sets out rules to make AI systems safer by requiring developers to follow strict security standards and test for vulnerabilities. It also creates oversight and enforcement mechanisms so that governments and organizations can keep AI technologies secure and prevent harmful misuse.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a new task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to identify and mitigate risks related to artificial intelligence. This task force will develop guidelines, coordinate with industry and government partners, and promote best practices to keep AI systems secure and trustworthy.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 aims to create clear rules for spotting, evaluating, and reducing risks in AI systems so they operate safely and securely. It requires companies to set up risk‑management plans, run regular security checks, and report any threats to protect people and maintain trust in AI technology.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes a framework for coordinating the design, deployment, and use of AI-driven physical systems to ensure safety, accountability, and public benefit. It requires oversight, standards, and collaboration between industry, government, and stakeholders to manage risks and promote responsible innovation.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to stop AI tools from producing fake or misleading information that could sway voters or undermine confidence in the electoral process. It sets rules for detecting AI‑generated content and imposes penalties for using such content to influence elections.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes regulatory requirements for overseeing AI systems that can autonomously enhance their own capabilities. It mandates continuous monitoring, reporting, and safety testing to prevent unintended behavior and ensure accountability.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building or expanding AI data centers to allow time for thorough assessment. This pause will let lawmakers evaluate the environmental, energy, and privacy impacts of large AI facilities and craft regulations that protect consumers and the planet.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law designed to prevent AI systems from acting independently in ways that could be harmful. It would establish safeguards, oversight, and penalties to ensure AI developers keep control and address any potential risks.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a federal board tasked with investigating and addressing cybersecurity risks that arise from the development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies. The board will gather evidence, analyze threats, and recommend policies to protect national security and public safety from AI‑related cyber attacks.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to ensure that advances in artificial intelligence benefit U.S. citizens by promoting safe, fair, and accessible AI technologies. It outlines measures to support workforce training, protect privacy, encourage responsible innovation, and provide oversight so AI serves public interests rather than just commercial gain.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires the government to systematically evaluate and publicize the capabilities, risks, and societal impacts of AI technologies. It aims to guide national AI strategy, promote ethical standards, and increase transparency in AI development and deployment.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 establishes that AI systems cannot diagnose or treat patients without the direct oversight of a licensed medical doctor. It requires that any AI tools used in healthcare must be supervised by a qualified physician, ensuring patient care decisions remain under human professional control.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy aims to create a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President to monitor, assess, and address risks from AI and other emerging technologies. It also establishes additional unspecified duties and responsibilities for that office in coordination with other federal agencies.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a new Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence. The committee will examine and oversee AI policy and development.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to create a systematic process for identifying and assessing the risks associated with AI technologies. It would require organizations to conduct risk evaluations, report their findings, and implement mitigation measures to protect public safety and privacy.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to regulate the development and use of artificial intelligence to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability. It outlines requirements for risk assessments, data governance, and oversight mechanisms to protect users and promote responsible AI innovation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at addressing the environmental footprint of AI technologies, such as energy consumption and electronic waste. It requires companies developing and deploying AI systems to assess and reduce their ecological impact, and establishes a reporting framework for transparency and accountability.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that aims to help schools teach students about artificial intelligence from kindergarten through high school. It sets standards and provides resources so teachers can give students a solid foundation in AI basics, use of AI tools, and responsible digital citizenship.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 sets rules to make sure AI research is trustworthy and safe. It requires researchers to test their models, share their methods openly, and follow government oversight so AI systems do not cause harm or unexpected problems.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to launch a pilot program that employs AI to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also mentions additional related actions, though those details are not specified.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 establishes a national framework to integrate artificial intelligence education into K‑12 schools. It mandates that schools develop curricula, train teachers, and provide students with the skills and tools needed to understand, responsibly use, and be prepared for an AI‑driven world.
